summary: Embedding cache invalidation delay causing rerank ordering skew and intermittent 503s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that rerank results for a production reranking route are intermittently returning degraded top-k order and correlated with short-lived 503 responses from the rerank endpoint. Impact: Search result relevance is inconsistent for a subset of queries and causes customer-facing errors (503) ~0.4% of requests over the last 48h. Environment: Dedicated deployment, us-east-1, pinned model redwood-reranker-v1 against an embeddings index backed by openembed-2-large vectors. Occurred following a config change to increase embedding cache TTL from 60s to 300s yesterday.

Observed behavior: 1) Rerank ordering shifts — previously stable top-3 reordering for same query set now shows different ordering intermittently. 2) Short 503 spikes on /v1/rerank for a few seconds, correlated with cache refresh windows. 3) Metrics show a small increase in p95 latency during those windows.

Expected behavior: Stable rerank ordering for identical inputs and no 5xx during normal cache refreshes.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer query corpus (attached as reproduction_queries.txt link in comments) against route /v1/rerank with same reranker/model pin. 2) Simulate embedding cache TTL change to 300s and observe rerank ordering over multiple runs across ~6 minute windows. 3) Observe intermittent 503s and order changes when cache shards refresh.
steps_to_reproduce: Replay customer query corpus via support repro harness (script provided)
Set embedding cache TTL to 300s in dedicated config and start a steady request stream (~200 QPS)
Watch rerank top-3 result ordering across consecutive runs and monitor /metrics and /health endpoints
logs: 2026-03-12T14:23:08Z WARN embedding-cache: shard-7 invalidate delayed by 320ms (expected <=50ms)
2026-03-12T14:23:09Z ERROR api-gateway: 503 response from reranker service for request id=4b1f2a (downstream timeout)
2026-03-12T14:23:09Z INFO reranker: fallback to cached-similarity path for request id=4b1f2a; similarities returned but order differs
comments: Support (Aisha): Opened with customer-provided repro and timeline. Noted that customer increased embedding cache TTL yesterday — suspect cache staleness/invalidation race.
SRE (Liam): Started correlating cache invalidation logs and rerank 5xx events. Initial hypothesis: cache shard invalidation is blocking upstream reranker threads causing timeouts.
Customer (StreamlineSearch): We rolled the TTL up because of upstream DB pressure. The effect started ~2 hours after the change. We can revert TTL if needed but want a more robust fix.

Eng (Maya Chen): Investigating whether cache refresh uses synchronous locks that block scorer threads. Pushing a branch to tune invalidation to async invalidation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1245
SRE (Liam): Observed that when a shard invalidation overruns, p95 latency increases 120ms and 503s spike. Workaround suggested: stagger cache refresh across shards and reduce TTL to 90s.
Support (Aisha): Shared suggested workaround with customer; asked for permission to schedule a canary with staggered refresh and TTL=90s in their dedicated fleet.
Customer (StreamlineSearch): Approved canary window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. Asked for post-canary metrics and longer-term remediation plan.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Synchronous cache invalidation holds locks on embedding index causing reranker scorer threads to block until invalidation completes.
Hypothesis 2: TTL increase caused bulk invalidations to align across many shards, producing a thundering-herd effect.

Evidence: Invalidation timestamps show many shard invalidations clustered within 200-400ms windows. CPU profiles show spikes in embed-cache worker threads and increased queue length for scorer worker pool.
Reproducer: Local repro with TTL=300s and stagger disabled reproduces ordering variance + occasional 503s at modest QPS (100-200).
Next steps: implement async invalidation (PR created), add jitter to shard refresh schedule, add backpressure on invalidation path to prevent blocking scorer threadpool, and run canary with customer.
resolution: In progress — temporary workaround applied: reduced embedding cache TTL to 90s and enabled staggered shard refresh on customer's dedicated fleet, which eliminated the 503 spikes in canary window. Long-term fix: merge async invalidation PR, add instrumentation to detect invalidation pileups, and add an automatic stagger/jitter mechanism. Plan to schedule rollout next week after QA. Customer will be notified of timeline.
follow_up_tasks: Merge and release async invalidation PR
Add metrics/alerts for invalidation clustering (dashboard + alert)
Add config option for auto-staggered cache refresh per deployment
Coordinate release and canary with StreamlineSearch ops team
customer_impact_summary: StreamlineSearch experienced intermittent rerank quality regressions (top-k reordering) and ~0.4% 503 responses during aligned cache refresh windows after TTL increase. Impacted user search relevance and caused customer-visible errors. Workaround reduced TTL and staggered refresh, mitigating the symptom for the customer.
